diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then a map $T:\Omega\to\Omega$ is a partition map if and only if $T\#\mathrm{Leb} = \hat{\mu}$, i.e. if it pushes the Lebesgue measure of $\Omega$ onto $\hat{\mu}$.
by choosing a test function $\phi$ which is equal to one on $\bm{x}_i$ and 0 on all the other $\bm{x}_j$, it is easily checked that $|T^{-1}(\{\bm{x}_i\})|=v_i$.

issues.failure_explanation: Equality of push-forward measures determines a map only up to Lebesgue-a.e. modification. Changing T on a null set preserves T#Leb=hat mu but can make the pointwise image leave {xi}; the proof's test-function argument only yields a.e. containment, not pointwise containment.

failure_location.quote: Reciprocally, if $T\#\mathrm{Leb} = \hat{\mu}$ then by choosing a test function whose support does not contain any $\bm{x}_i$, one can see that the image set of $T$ is contained in $\{\bm{x}_i\}_i$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State partition maps and optimizers up to a.e. equality and fix a convention on the zero-measure intersections of cells.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's iff statement and the pointwise uniqueness of the Monge partition map in the following theorem are not literally valid as written.
issues.title: Push-forward characterisation of partition maps is not pointwise
issues.why_classification: This is the standard a.e. qualification in optimal transport; it is a local repair that preserves all substantive conclusions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\mathscr{L}_i := \{x\in \Omega\,:\,c(\bm{x},\bm{x}_i) - w_i \leq c(\bm{x},\bm{x}_j) - w_j \,\,\,\forall j\}$.
return as output the unique vector of optimal values for the Kantorovitch potentials $(w_1, \dots, w_N)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The Laguerre cells depend only on the differences w_i-w_j. Adding the same constant to every w_i leaves all cells unchanged, so the vector of potentials cannot be uniquely defined as stated.

failure_location.quote: The intersection of two Laguerre cells has zero Lebesgue measure and the weights $w_i\in \mathbb{R}$, called Kantorovich potentials, are uniquely defined such that for all $i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that the Kantorovich potentials are unique up to an additive constant, or impose a normalization such as w_1=0.
issues.overall_effect: The uniqueness part of the semi-discrete theorem, and the sentence claiming that solvers return a unique vector of potentials, are false as written.
issues.title: Kantorovich potentials claimed unique instead of unique up to additive constant
issues.why_classification: A one-line uniqueness-up-to-constant correction is routine and does not weaken the cell or volume construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The shape $\mathscr{S}\subset\Omega$ that minimizes the individual energy
$\mathscr{S}(w) = \{\bm{x}\in\Omega,\,\, c(\bm{x},\bm{x}_i) \leq w\}$,

issues.failure_explanation: For a general nonnegative cost, U(0) need not be 0 (the cost may vanish on a positive-measure set), and the distribution function w↦|{c≤w}| may have jumps or plateaus. Then there may be no w with |{c≤w}|=v_i, and a volume-constrained minimizer may require taking an arbitrary measurable subset of a level set.

failure_location.quote: First of all, since the function $U : w \mapsto |\mathscr{S}(w)|$ is non-decreasing, $U(0)=0$ and $U(w)\to1$ as $w\to+\infty$ there exists a unique $w^*>0$ such that $U(w^*) = v_i$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an assumption that the level-set volume function is continuous and strictly increasing at the target volume, or replace the minimizer by a generalized sublevel set including an arbitrary subset of the critical level.
issues.overall_effect: The general preferred-shape statement is not supported; it is valid only under additional regularity/non-atomicity assumptions on the cost distribution.
issues.title: Preferred-shape lemma assumes an exact sublevel set exists
issues.why_classification: The costs actually used in the paper can satisfy such an assumption; the repair is a local qualification rather than a new construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A drawback of our discretization procedure is that there is generally no Monge map between two discrete measures.
$j^* := \argmin_{i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}}\{c(\bm{y}_j,\bm{x}_i)-w_i\}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposed map sends each pixel atom of mass 1/M entirely to one target. Its pushforward therefore has target masses that are integer multiples of 1/M. For arbitrary volumes v_i, no hard allocation map can satisfy T#hat mu_0=hat mu, and the argmin rule does not repair this because the true discrete optimal plan generally splits source atoms.

failure_location.quote: As a replacement for the Monge map defined in Theorem~\ref{thm:semidiscrete}, we consider the following discrete allocation map

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either use the soft optimal transport plan (allowing pixel splitting), restrict to v_i that are multiples of 1/M with an exact matching, or explicitly state that the hard allocation is an approximation of the volume constraint.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete shape construction does not literally deliver the strict volume constraint claimed for the pixel-discrete model; it is at best an approximation unless extra integrality conditions are imposed.
issues.title: Hard discrete allocation map cannot in general enforce the pixel masses
issues.why_classification: The repair is local but changes the discrete input-output contract from strict volume preservation to an approximation or to an additional integrality restriction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $c$ be a cost function such that for all particle $i$, $c_i : y\in \Omega \mapsto c(y,\bm{x}_i)\in [0,+\infty) $ belongs to $C^{1,1}(\Omega)$.
when $\alpha<1$, the cost is a concave function of the distance, which allows larger deformations and potentially shapes far from the base ball shape.

issues.failure_explanation: The semi-discrete theorem invoked for the Laguerre partition assumes each c_i is C^{1,1} on Omega. The power cost |y-x|^alpha is not C^{1,1} at y=x for 0<alpha<2 (and not C^1 for alpha≤1). Thus the theorem does not establish the claimed unique continuous partition for the soft regimes used in the paper, such as alpha=0.75 and alpha=1.

failure_location.quote: For any value of the parameter $\alpha$, the base shape of the particles is always a ball.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict the continuous theorem to alpha≥2 and provide a separate discrete/finite-dimensional justification for the numerical method, or state that the soft-regime simulations are numerical heuristics not covered by the cited C^{1,1} result.
issues.overall_effect: The formal optimal-transport justification of the Laguerre shapes and strict volume constraint is missing for a central advertised deformability regime.
issues.title: Power costs with 0<alpha<2 are used outside the C^{1,1} theorem
issues.why_classification: A supported repair can keep the numerical method but weakens the formal scope; it does not require a new global architecture, but the advertised arbitrary-deformability theorem guarantee is materially affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: associated to the base $L^2$ cost $c_0(\bm{x},\bm{x}_i) = |\bm{x}-\bm{x}_i|^2/R_0^2$ (for simplicity).
$c_i : y\in \Omega \mapsto c(y,\bm{x}_i)\in [0,+\infty) $

issues.failure_explanation: The costs used in the paper are allowed to be zero, and the base L2 cost is exactly zero at x=xi. Hence -log c takes the value -∞ at those points and is not a real-valued potential. The subsequent perturbation and PDE-like interpretation are ill-defined without regularization or a strictly positive cost.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace -log c by -log(c+epsilon), -log(max(c,epsilon)), or otherwise assume a strictly positive cost and state the regularization.
issues.overall_effect: The logarithmic-potential modeling device introduced for surface fluctuations is not well-defined for the stated base costs.
issues.title: Logarithmic cost potential is undefined where the cost vanishes
issues.why_classification: This is a local regularity fix that does not alter the main optimal-transport construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \[\varphi(\bm{x},\bm{x}_i) = - \log c(\bm{x},\bm{x}_i).\]
f(\delta) = -\delta_+,

issues.failure_explanation: Since phi=-log c, decreasing phi increases c (c=e^{-phi}). The perturbation f=-delta_+ lowers phi in directions of positive gradient, which raises the cost there rather than lowering it, so it does not 'allow deformations' as claimed. The sign convention in the chemotaxis perturbation is inconsistent with the definition of the logarithmic potential.

failure_location.quote: which corresponds to lowering the potential and thus allowing deformations in the directions of large nonnegative gradients.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either define the perturbation with the opposite sign (e.g. f=+delta_+ for the elongated case) or define the potential as +log c and adjust the interpretation accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The stated mechanism by which the elongated and fan-like chemotaxis shapes are produced is reversed or unsupported.
issues.title: Sign of logarithmic potential perturbation contradicts the claimed deformation effect
issues.why_classification: A sign correction is local and can preserve the intended modelling mechanism if applied consistently.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \[\dd\xi_k = -\xi_k\dd t + \dd B^k_t,\]
that is, protrusions are created randomly and naturally retract.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed SDE is an unreflected Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with stationary Gaussian law and sample paths that cross zero. It therefore does not implement the stated constraint xi_k≥0.

failure_location.quote: We assume that the elongation range (amplitude) of the protrusion $\xi_k$ is constrained by $\xi_k\geq0$ and follows the stochastic differential equation

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a reflected Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, a CIR-type SDE with nonnegative state space, or explicitly set xi_k=|...| and state the resulting dynamics.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \bm{\vec{F}}_{\bm{z}_{ijk}\to i} = \left(\bm{\vec{\gamma}}_{ij}\cdot \frac{\bm{z} - \bm{x}_i}{|\bm{z} - \bm{x}_i|}\right)\frac{\bm{z} - \bm{x}_i}{|\bm{z} - \bm{x}_i|},
\bm{\vec{\gamma}}_{ijk} = \bm{\vec{\gamma}}_{ij} + \bm{\vec{\gamma}}_{jk} + \bm{\vec{\gamma}}_{ki},

issues.failure_explanation: A linear spring force between centroid xi and junction z would be proportional to z-xi with a stiffness, not to the radial projection of a single edge tension gamma_ij. The preceding junction force is the vector sum gamma_ijk, but the displayed formula uses only gamma_ij. In the later dynamics the double sum over j and k also counts the same triple junction multiple times unless an unordered-distinct convention is added.

failure_location.quote: We simply assume a linear spring force between the centroids and the junction points, which can be interpreted as a very basic cytoskeleton model.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define one net junction force (e.g. based on gamma_ijk), state a clear projection or spring law, and sum over unordered distinct triples or introduce a factor that avoids double counting.
issues.overall_effect: The surface-interaction dynamics that include triple-junction forces is not the mathematical model described in the prose.
issues.title: Triple-junction force formula does not match the stated spring or junction force
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained but requires correcting the force law and summation convention; as written the construction is not the one claimed.

volumes denoted by $\mathcal{V}_N = (v_1,\ldots,v_N)$

The subsequent first-variation scaling and mean-field limit are therefore stated for a restricted equal-volume system, not for the general model described earlier.

failure_location.quote: The main idea, which originates from statistical physics, is to consider the limit of the sequence of random empirical measures $\hat{\mu} \equiv \hat{\mu}_N := \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N \delta_{\bm{x}_i}$ when $N\to+\infty$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \[|\det( \nabla T)| = f.\]
\[\det(\mathrm{I} - \nabla^2\Phi) = \pm f.\]

issues.failure_explanation: For a map T satisfying T#f=Leb, the change-of-variables formula gives |det DT(x)|=1/f(x), not f(x). In the L2 case with T=x-nabla Phi, the displayed equation should involve |det(I-nabla^2 Phi)|=1/f (up to the standard regularity assumptions). The general determinant formula is also not the correct Hessian of the composition of ell^* with nabla Phi. Hence the announced coupled Fokker-Planck-Monge-Ampere system is not supported by the displayed derivation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the Monge-Ampere density relation to the reciprocal Jacobian, derive the correct general-cost determinant equation, or explicitly present the system as a heuristic with no claimed validity.
issues.overall_effect: The formal mean-field PDE system in the supplementary section is mathematically incorrect as written and cannot be taken as a derived limit equation.
issues.title: Formal Fokker-Planck-Monge-Ampere equation has the density relation inverted
issues.why_classification: The repair is confined to the supplementary formal section but requires correcting a nontrivial PDE derivation; the main computational claims survive, while the advertised formal mean-field system does not as written.
